item.title: Heavy Rain
item.description:
The high-pressure system from China covers upper Thailand and the South China Sea leading to the easterly and southeasterly winds bring the moisture from the South China Sea and the Gulf to the upper country with more rain and isolated heavy rain are likely in the lower North, the lower Northeast, the Central including Bangkok and its vicinity and the East and the upper South. The southwest monsoon prevails over the Andaman Sea while the monsoon trough lies across the lower South with isolated heavy rains in the South.
In the Andaman Sea and the Gulf, the waves will be higher than 2 meters high in thundershower areas.
item.author: info_service@tmd.mail.go.th (Thai Meteorological Department)

item.title: Very Heavy Rain
item.description: The high-pressure system from China extended to the North, the Northeast and the South China Sea while the easterly and southeasterly winds bring the moisture from the South China Sea and the Gulf to the lower part of the Northeast, the East and the lower Central. Meanwhile, the monsoon trough lies across the middle South. Variable weather with thundershower, gusty wind and isolated heavy rains are forecast in the North and the Central while isolated heavy to very heavy rains are possible in the South. In the Andaman Sea and the Gulf, the waves will be higher than 2 meters high in thundershower areas.
item.author: info_service@tmd.mail.go.th (Thai Meteorological Department)

item.title: Very Heavy Rain
item.description:
Another high-pressure system from China extended to the upper North and the upper Northeast while the easterly wind and the southeasterly wind bring moisture from the South China Sea to the eastern part of the Northeast and the East. Meanwhile, the monsoon trough lies across the Gulf and the South.
More rains and variable weather with thundershower, gust wind, hail and isolated heavy to very heavy rainfall including lightning strike are likely in the upper country while isolated heavy rains remains in the South. After that less rain are possible in the upper North and the upper Northeast.
The Andaman Sea and the Gulf, waves will be higher than 2 meters high in thundershower areas.
item.author: info_service@tmd.mail.go.th (Thai Meteorological Department)

item.title: Heavy Rain
item.description:
Another high-pressure system from China extends to upper Vietnam and upper Laos, expected to extend to the upper North and the upper Northeast by today (10 October 2026) while the easterly wind and the southeasterly wind bring moisture from the South China Sea to the eastern part of the Northeast and the East. Meanwhile, the monsoon trough lies across the Gulf and the South. More rains and variable weather with thundershower, gust wind, hail and isolated heavy to very heavy rainfall including lightning strike are likely in the upper country while isolated heavy rains remains in the South.
The Andaman Sea and the Gulf, waves will be higher than 2 meters high in thundershower areas.
item.author: info_service@tmd.mail.go.th (Thai Meteorological Department)

item.title: Heavy Rain
item.description: Another high-pressure system from China extends to upper Vietnam, expected to extend to the upper North and the upper Northeast by today (10 October 2026) while the easterly wind and the southeasterly wind bring the moisture from the South China Sea to the eastern part of the Northeast and the East. Meanwhile, the monsoon trough lies across the Gulf and the South. More rains and variable weather with thundershower, gust wind, hail and isolated heavy to very heavy rainfall including lightning strike are likely in the upper country while isolated heavy rains remains in the South. People should beware of severe conditions with heavy to very heavy rainfalls and accumulations that may cause flash flood and overflows, especially along the waterways near foothills and lowlands. The Andaman Sea and the Gulf, waves will be higher than 2 meters high in thundershower areas. All ships should keep off thundershowers.
item.author: info_service@tmd.mail.go.th (Thai Meteorological Department)
